leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight round-1 files put B001 (magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene and moire quantum matter) alone in the preferred configuration, all with the same three names: MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer. They share the case that a quantitative prediction (the 2011 continuum model) was followed by an experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states and by independent reproduction. They also share the view that the pairing mechanism should not be part of the citation. They differ in how heavily they weigh the open mechanism and fast-moving field, in how they would handle the experimental credit given a single experimental name, and in citation wording (some credit the prediction and the phases; Danielsson and Johansson stress that the citation must not claim an explanation of the superconductivity). Johansson and Olsson moved to B001 from fourth place and from a first-place B030 ranking respectively, and Mehlig moved from a two-name to a three-name proposal. Kroll and Lindroth name B001 only as an alternative.

Two members put B007 (optical lattice clocks, Katori and Ye) alone in the preferred configuration, with identical names and near-identical citations on magic-wavelength trapping and the 1e-18 level. Their case rests on a sharply defined invention, a two-person attribution that is clean on the supplied names, independent multi-laboratory confirmation and stable interpretation. They differ in emphasis: Kroll stresses that the capability to measure changed, Lindroth also weighs the distinction from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize. Both rank B001 as their first alternative. Six other members list B007 as an alternative (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce), so it is a common fallback rather than a lead for them. The chair counts only what is explicit in the files.

areas_of_agreement: B001 and B007 are the two candidates every file treats as serious: each member either prefers one of them alone or lists one of them as an alternative, and no member argues that either is scientifically weak.

All eight members propose the same two names for B007 (Katori and Ye) in their opening proposals, and no round-1 file contests that pair; the credit concerns raised concern other lattice-clock groups and ultrastable-laser infrastructure outside the pair.

Members on both sides of the B001/B007 split state that the existence of the flat-band correlated and superconducting phases has been reproduced by independent groups, and that the unresolved pairing mechanism is a separate question from the discovery.
No member proposes a multi-part prize in the preferred configurations, and Johansson, Kroll and Olsson note that combining B001 with B007 would exceed the three-name limit.
Six of the eight files keep Bistritzer alongside MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, and Mehlig has moved from two names to three, so no round-1 file now prefers a two-name B001.
scientific_disputes: Whether the discovery recognised in B001 is the existence of flat-band correlated and superconducting phases at the predicted angle (Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce) or whether an unsettled interpretation of the correlated states and superconductivity leaves the lasting content unfixed (Kroll, Lindroth).

Whether a lattice clock is a distinct achievement or an improvement on a line already honoured by the 2005 frequency comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize (Lindroth raises this as her main reservation; Danielsson argues B001 opens a new class of matter while B007 refines an honoured field).

Whether the criterion should favour scientific novelty and field-opening breadth (B001) or an enabling measurement capability with concrete payoffs (B007); Kroll and Eriksson dispute whether this is a difference of values or of evidence.

Whether B015 and B008 belong in the discussion at all, since Lindroth and Kroll list B015 as an alternative while Mehlig argues a theory-only prize is harder to justify than a prediction tested by experiment, and Zoller appears in both B008 and B015.
attribution_disputes: B001 experimental side: Jarillo-Herrero is the only experimental name, while Cao (first author), Fatemi and the Dean, Efetov, Young and Yazdani groups fall outside the three-name limit; Danielsson, Eriksson and Johansson argue the group leader convention is defensible, while Kroll and Mehlig note the limit cannot do justice to the field.

B001 theory side: members agree Bistritzer should stay with MacDonald because of the joint 2011 paper, but Olsson raises earlier twisted-graphene band-structure theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto, Suarez Morell) and Mehlig notes precursors, which bear on how the citation should be worded.

B007: the pair Katori and Ye is uncontested among the eight, but Kroll and Lindroth note that other Sr and Yb lattice-clock groups and ultrastable-laser contributors sit outside it, and Lindroth says Ye's contribution is distinct from the comb work.

B058 and B030: Wallraff (and for Eriksson also Devoret) is outside the credited names for B058, and Krivanek is outside the credited names for B030; several members cite these as defects that the supplied names cannot repair.

B039 (my own alternative): I note individual credit inside the large IceCube collaboration is unresolved and my own proposal names only Halzen and Karle while the other proposals name Spiering as well.
maturity_disputes: B001: eight years since the 2018 discovery is regarded as mature by Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce, but Kroll, Lindroth and Johansson (in his case against) point to the open pairing mechanism, twist-angle variability and a fast-moving field as reasons a committee could wait.

B007: Kroll and Lindroth treat the independent confirmation as complete, while Olsson, Eriksson and Lindroth herself note that the formal SI redefinition of the second has not happened, so part of the claimed impact is prospective; Kroll says it should not carry the argument.

B058: Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Olsson and Pearce treat the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits as an adjacent-recognition timing problem, while the scientific weight of circuit QED is not disputed in the files.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Kroll: documented research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder and a possible personal and institutional link to Jun Ye through JILA, relevant to B007; he suggests explicit disclosure or possible recusal on B007 and records no link to Katori. Lindroth says the Hall link is a point for transparency, not grounds to discount the case.

Johansson: directs WACQT and works at Chalmers in superconducting circuits, so B058 (and less directly B015) is in his own field; he states he would recuse himself from discussion centred on B058 beyond field-specific information.

Olsson: B030 (electron optics) lies in her own research field and she ranked it first in her opening; she would recuse on B030 if the committee judged that necessary. She also records a University of Tokyo fellowship as a possible but undocumented link to B007 (Katori) and shares Chalmers with Johansson.
Lindroth: proximity to ETH Zurich and to atomic theory around Zoller and Cirac may warrant disclosure if B008 or B015 were taken up; no recusal is proposed for B007.

Pearce (chair): field proximity to B039 (IceCube) through astroparticle instrumentation; documented collaborations are PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur, not IceCube, and no recusal issue is identified.
Danielsson, Eriksson and Mehlig record no specific conflict for the leading candidates; Danielsson and Mehlig note that their own fields are outside condensed matter.
questions_for_round2: For B001, does the committee want a citation that credits only the flat-band prediction and the observation of the correlated insulating and superconducting phases, and who among Cao, Fatemi or other experimental groups, if anyone, should be reconsidered within the three-name limit?

How much should the unresolved pairing mechanism and still-debated correlated states in twisted bilayer graphene count against B001 on maturity, and what specific evidence would members who rank it fourth need to move it up?

Between B001 and B007, is the committee ranking by field-opening scientific novelty or by enabling measurement capability and cleanliness of attribution, and can the six B001 supporters and the two B007 supporters state which criterion decides in this case?

Is the pending formal redefinition of the second a condition of maturity for B007, an adjacent policy matter, or irrelevant, and does the 2005 comb prize and 2012 ion-control prize make the lattice clock sufficiently distinct?
Does Kroll's disclosed link to John Hall's laboratory, and through JILA to Jun Ye, require recusal on B007, or only disclosure, and how should the committee record it?
Johansson, Kroll and Olsson note that B001 and B007 cannot be combined within three names; is there any member who would support a two-part configuration, and if so which names would be dropped?
summary.chair_observation: The round-1 files show a clear but not unanimous lead: six members explicitly prefer B001 alone and two prefer B007 alone, with each group naming the other candidate as its first or second alternative. The open items are the credit on the experimental side of B001, how much weight the unsettled superconducting mechanism carries, and whether the committee prefers field-opening discovery or a clean enabling invention with a pending policy payoff. I record these as process points and not as a ruling.
